# 12 — Launch protection

<!-- generated:status-banner -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-doc-assets.mjs. Do not edit inside this block. -->

> **RC6 is LIVE AND OPEN ON THREE CHAINS.** RC6 is deployed and PUBLIC on Ethereum (1), Base (8453) and Robinhood Chain (4663): all three accept ordinary, permissionless creator launches. The factory is the same CREATE2 address on all three. RC6 is NOT deployed on BNB Smart Chain (56), which is deferred, and no date is set for it.
> Public creator launch is **open** on Ethereum (1), Base (8453), Robinhood Chain (4663) and **closed** on the other 1 configured chain.
> See [08 — Status and limitations](08-status.md).

<!-- /generated:status-banner -->

Every RC6 launch elects, once and permanently, whether the first minutes of its market are priced
differently from every minute after them. This page is what that election means.

It is a **creator choice**, not a platform guarantee. An earlier generation of this documentation
said protection was mandatory with no opt-out. That is retired: the owner amendment of
2026-08-16 made it an election, and the contract now admits two modes. What stayed mandatory is
narrower and worth stating plainly — **every launch must declare a mode**, no launch may omit the
field, and neither mode has an exemption for anybody.

## The mechanism, before the modes

The canonical pool is initialized with Uniswap v4's `DYNAMIC_FEE_FLAG`, and the project's art hook
returns a per-swap LP-fee override from `beforeSwap` with `OVERRIDE_FEE_FLAG` set.

That is Uniswap's own dynamic-fee mechanism and nothing else. It is **not** an ERC-20 transfer tax,
**not** a proprietary-router toll, **not** a return-delta skim, and **not** a separate sniper-tax
vault. The hook takes no custody of the proceeds: the fee accrues to the pool position exactly as
any LP fee does, and is then split like any other collected fee
([06 — Fees and revenue](06-fees-and-revenue.md)).

The consequence worth understanding is that there is no route around it. `PoolManager` applies the
override inside `Pool.swap`, so the identical fee is charged through the RELICS interface, the
Universal Router, a direct `unlock` + `swap`, an aggregator, a searcher bundle and a private
orderflow relay alike — because the callback is a property of the pool's own key.

## The three enum values, and why one of them is not a choice

<!-- generated:launch-protection -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-doc-assets.mjs. Do not edit inside this block. -->

| Mode | Enum | Creator may elect | Buy-side LP fee | Sell-side LP fee | What it is |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `UNSPECIFIED` | 0 | **not selectable** | — | — | The enum-zero sentinel. It is what an unset field, an omitted argument and a default-constructed value all read as, so it means nobody chose. `bind` refuses it, the fee path treats it as the maximum rather than the minimum, and it must never be rendered as NONE. |
| `NONE` | 1 | selectable | 1% flat, from the first block | 1% flat | A flat 1% LP fee in both directions from the first block. No window, no decay, no countdown. A project on this mode must never be described as protected, sniper-resistant or fair-launched. |
| `PROTECTED_98_MINUTES` | 2 | selectable | 99% → 1% over 98 min | 1% flat | The buy-side LP fee falls from 99% to 1% across 5,880 seconds of wall-clock time from the moment the pool opens. The sell side is a flat 1% throughout, including the first second. |

**Schedule:** `fee = BASE + floor(ADDON * max(DURATION - elapsed, 0) / DURATION), clamped to [BASE, MAX_EFFECTIVE_BUY]`, with
`BASE = 10000` pips, `ADDON = 980000` pips,
`MAX_EFFECTIVE_BUY = 990000` pips and `DURATION = 5880` s
(pips of the swap input; `1000000` pips = 100%).

**Anchor:** POOL_INITIALIZATION. The window belongs to the pool, in every launch mode. A bonding-curve project's pool is created at finalization, so it opens at the maximum fee however long the sale ran first.

**Exemptions:** NONE. beforeSwap reads nothing about who is swapping - not sender, not tx.origin, not hookData - so an exemption is inexpressible rather than merely refused. Creator, platform, deployer, Safe, routers and aggregators pay the same schedule.

**Mutable after launch:** no.
**Protection mandatory:** no — it is a creator election.
**Studio default:** `PROTECTED_98_MINUTES`; electing `NONE` requires an explicit acknowledgement.

<!-- /generated:launch-protection -->

`UNSPECIFIED` sits at enum zero deliberately. Solidity zero-initialises storage, so if `NONE`
occupied slot zero then "nobody plumbed the election through" and "the creator chose no protection"
would be the same bytes — and every missed field or truncated header would silently produce an
unprotected launch that looked deliberate. With the sentinel at zero, the same failure produces a
value the contract refuses outright.

**Never render `UNSPECIFIED` as `NONE`.** They are one enum position apart and read almost the same
in prose, and the difference is the whole product: `NONE` is a creator who deliberately launched
without protection and acknowledged a disclosure saying so; `UNSPECIFIED` is a field nobody set.

## The curve

![Buy-side LP fee against minutes since the pool opened: with PROTECTED_98_MINUTES the buy fee falls from 99% to 1% over 98 minutes, while with NONE it is a flat 1% from the first block; the sell fee is a flat 1% in both modes, drawn on the same line as the unprotected buy fee because they are the same number.](../assets/launch-protection.svg)

The same values, as text:

<!-- generated:launch-protection-checkpoints -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-doc-assets.mjs. Do not edit inside this block. -->

| Minutes since the pool opened | Seconds | Buy-side LP fee (`PROTECTED_98_MINUTES`) | Buy-side LP fee (`NONE`) | Sell-side LP fee (both) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 0 | 99% | 1% | 1% |
| 1 | 60 | 98% | 1% | 1% |
| 10 | 600 | 89% | 1% | 1% |
| 30 | 1800 | 69% | 1% | 1% |
| 60 | 3600 | 39% | 1% | 1% |
| 90 | 5400 | 9% | 1% | 1% |
| 98 | 5880 | 1% | 1% | 1% |
| 98+ | 5880+ | 1% | 1% | 1% |

<!-- /generated:launch-protection-checkpoints -->

Two properties of that table are easy to misread.

**The decaying quantity is the add-on, not the span.** The hook computes
`BASE + floor(ADDON × remaining ÷ DURATION)`. Rebuilding the curve as
`MAX − floor(span × elapsed ÷ DURATION)` agrees at both endpoints and differs by one pip almost
everywhere in between, because the floor falls on the other side. That is a small error and still a
number on a buy screen that the chain disagrees with, so derive from the add-on form.

**The window is wall-clock, never block count.** RC6 targets four chains with four different block
times and the promise is stated in minutes; `block.timestamp` is the only quantity that means the
same thing on all of them.

## Where the window starts

The anchor is **pool initialization**, in every launch mode, read from the hook's own
`poolOpenedAt` — written once by `PoolManager` inside `afterInitialize`.

There is deliberately no mode branch. A bonding-curve project's pool is created at finalization, so
it opens at the maximum fee however long the sale ran beforehand: a pool that has never traded gets
its own window, because its opening price is one the sale never set. And because
`finalizeSale` is permissionless, an escrow-anchored window would have let a buyer who skipped the
sale entirely finalize it himself and take the pool's whole opening ascent at the base fee, at a
block of his choosing.

A bonding-curve launch therefore has **two phases that are not the same strength**, and a single
"protected" badge across both is wrong:

| Phase | What is happening | Decay countdown |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Curve phase | A rising unit cost along the published curve. It prices **size**; it rations nothing, identifies nobody, and one buyer can still take the whole curve. | No — there is no pool yet |
| Pool phase | The elected schedule, running from the moment the canonical pool is initialized | Only if the elected mode is `PROTECTED_98_MINUTES` |

## Two hook generations, and only one of them is current

The launch-protection schedule belongs to the RC6 hook. Getting these two numbers the wrong way
round is a truthfulness failure in either direction, so both are stated with their status.

| Generation | Permission mask | Status | LP fee model |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RC5 | `0x1440` | **Deployed, superseded** — RC5 hooks still hold code, and `0x1440` is also the mask of the live flagship RELICS collection hook on Ethereum mainnet. No launch made today binds one | Static pool fee |
| RC6 | `0x14C0` | **Deployed and current** — every launch on Ethereum, Base and Robinhood Chain binds this generation | Dynamic LP fee set in `beforeSwap` |

Read the context before copying either number. `0x1440` is correct for RC5 and for the flagship
collection, and wrong for an RC6 launchpad hook.

The RC6 pool is initialized with Uniswap v4's dynamic-fee sentinel, `0x800000`, in
`PoolKey.fee`. That sentinel **is not a fee**: it means "this pool's LP fee is set at runtime by its
hook". A `PoolKey` carrying it hashes to a different `PoolId` than the same pool described with a
concrete fee, which is the likeliest integration mistake against a dynamic-fee generation.

## Launch modes: which ones a creator may elect

Launch protection governs the canonical pool. Which launch mode gets a project to that pool is a
separate election, and the two are asked separately.

| Launch mode | May a creator elect it? |
| --- | --- |
| `INSTANT_V4` | yes |
| `BONDING_CURVE_SALE_TO_V4` | yes |
| `FIXED_PRICE_SALE_TO_V4` | no |

**Why `FIXED_PRICE_SALE_TO_V4` is not offered.** The fixed-price sale phase does not limit how much of a sale any one buyer can take: there is no per-buyer cap, no cooldown and no maximum per transaction. The launch-protection schedule cannot apply there, because it governs the Uniswap v4 pool and that pool does not exist until the sale finalizes. This mode is therefore not offered.

The name stays in the wire format because launch modes are an on-chain enum and removing a member
renumbers the ones after it, which would silently change what an already-written bundle means. The
creator kit refuses a bundle electing it at `relics validate` and `relics export`, and the deployed
sale contract refuses it at launch for every caller.

## What the liquidity claim is, and what it is not

The claim worth making is narrow, and it is the only one the bytecode supports:

> Genesis liquidity is held by the immutable locker and cannot be withdrawn through the deployed locker.

That is a statement about the locker's bytecode, not about every risk. Surrounding protocol components are upgradeable by a 2-of-3 Safe with no timelock, token prices can fall to nothing, and a creator can behave badly in ways no contract prevents.

Those two paragraphs travel together as well. A wider sentence would be easier to write and would
not be true.

## No exemptions, and why that is structural

Creator, `ProjectRights` holder, payout recipient, collaborator, splitter, deployment wallet,
protocol Safe, treasury, agent wallet, the RELICS front end, an approved router and an affiliate
all pay the same schedule. There is no allowlist, no `isInitialPurchase` carve-out and no secret
route.

The absence is structural rather than promised: `beforeSwap` reads **nothing** about who is
swapping — not `sender`, not `tx.origin`, not `hookData` — so an exemption is not merely refused,
it is inexpressible. Other launchpads exempt the creator's first buy. This one cannot.

Every number in the schedule is a compile-time constant with no setter, no admin and no upgrade
path, and the only stored input is the pool's opening timestamp. The Safe cannot change a launched
schedule; neither can the creator, the caller, or calldata.

## What it does, and what it does not do

**What it does.** For the first minutes of a market, buying costs a multiple of what the same buy
costs later. That removes the advantage of being first in the block, because being first is exactly
when the fee is highest.

**What it does not do.** It does not guarantee equal allocation, it does not identify anyone, and
it does not stop a buyer from waiting for the fee to fall and then buying. It prices the first
minutes; it does not decide who is allowed to transact in them.

Those two paragraphs travel together. The second is not a footnote to the first.

### Claims that are false, in either mode

Do not write, and do not let an interface imply:

- "sniping is impossible", "cannot be sniped", "snipe-proof", "sniper-proof"
- "bots cannot buy", "no bot can …"
- "perfectly fair", "guaranteed fair distribution", "fair launch"
- "Sybil-resistant" — neither mode identifies anybody, and splitting across addresses costs gas

And for a `NONE` project specifically, never "protected", "launch protected", "protection is
active", "the fee decays from 99%", or a countdown of any kind. A `NONE` pool has no window, so
there is no instant at which one ends.

## Which mode a creator gets by default

The studio defaults a **draft** to `PROTECTED_98_MINUTES`, and electing `NONE` requires ticking an
explicit acknowledgement that clears again on every mode change.

That asymmetry is deliberate, because the failure modes are not symmetric. A creator who wanted no
protection and got it by default has a market that costs early buyers more than they intended for
98 minutes. A creator who wanted protection and got `NONE` by default has no recourse at all, and
neither do their buyers.

A **final bundle may not default.** A draft is a work in progress; a final bundle is the artifact a
creator signs, and the mode is an immutable economic property of the market it creates. A bundle
that does not name a mode is refused at export and again at simulation — before any wallet is
touched, so no gas is spent on a project whose protection nobody chose.

## What an integrator must read

- `antiSnipeMode()` on the hook — the election, as the enum. Decode zero as `UNSPECIFIED`, never as
  `NONE`, and treat an out-of-range value as a contract you were not built for rather than guessing.
- `antiSnipeEndsAt()` — zero on an unprotected pool, and that zero is a **statement**, not a missing
  value. Read the mode first; a countdown rendered from that zero is a countdown to nothing.
- `currentBuyFeePips()` / `buyFeePipsAt(timestamp)` / `currentSellFeePips()` — the schedule, servable
  for any instant so a front end, an indexer or an auditor can plot the whole curve without
  restating it. A restated curve is a curve that drifts.

Recompute the buy fee continuously in the browser. A fee that is only correct at page load is
exactly the fee a buyer discovers after signing.
